ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory adverse-media, PEP, and sanctions screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List executed through the United Nations Act 1946 (NZ); (ii) the New Zealand Sanctions Register under the Sanctions Act 2022 (NZ); (iii) the OFAC SDN List and related US sanctions programs applicable to USD SWIFT wire and ACH payment rails; (iv) the NZ Police and SIS designated terrorist lists under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002 (NZ); and (v) domestic and foreign politically exposed person databases under s 5 and Part 2 of the AML/CFT Act 2009. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where the counterparty or fund source originates from a high-risk third country identified by FATF; a documented negative-match screening certificate must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register — Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), online name search and reservation portal at https://company-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz, with NZBN assignment through https://www.business.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Latin-script English characters; Māori orthography (including macrons) is accepted; the default legal suffix for a limited-liability International Company is 'Limited' or 'Ltd' unless an exemption is granted under s 24(2) of the Companies Act 1993; a reserved or registered name must not be identical or almost identical to any existing name on the Companies Register or to a reserved name, must not mislead as to the company's activities, and must not contain restricted or protected words absent prior ministerial approval.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank (requires prior consent of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand)
Insurance / Assurance (requires prior consent under the Insurance (Prudential Supervision) Act 2010)
Trust / Trustee (subject to sectoral licensing objections for trust service providers)
University (requires Minister of Education approval under the Education and Training Act 2020)
ANZAC (protected under the Flags, Emblems, and Names Protection Act 1981)
Royal / Crown / Government / Ministry / National (implies Crown or governmental connection and is disallowed under s 22 of the Companies Act 1993)
Incorporated (restricted to incorporated societies and charities, not trading companies)
Chartered (requires professional body approval, e.g., chartered accountancy institutes)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Registrar declines to reserve a name under ss 22-25 of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request through the Companies Office within 10 working days of the refusal, attaching supporting submissions and any ministerial or supervisory consents for restricted words; if the internal reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may initiate an administrative appeal or judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 (NZ) within the applicable limitation period, and may concurrently reserve and lodge a compliant alternative name so the incorporation timeline is not delayed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or serviced-office address is permissible for this low-risk Programmatic AdTech SSP entity provided it is a real physical address within New Zealand, staffed during ordinary business hours, and capable of accepting service of process under s 188 of the Companies Act 1993; a post-office-box-only address is not acceptable, but a registered-agent virtual address that meets these conditions will satisfy the statutory registered-office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 2–5% per annum) for a non-licensed, tax-exempt international company; unannounced on-site inspections are not routine for an AD-exchange SSP platform and would likely arise only upon adverse AML/CFT intelligence, sanctions-list exposure, or a Department of Internal Affairs / FMA compliance review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), principally sections 10 (essential requirements of a company), 12 (incorporation application), 13 (consents of shareholders and directors), 14 (company name restrictions), 15 (registered office), 16 (constitution), 17 (certificate of incorporation), 91 to 96 (appointment and duties of directors) and 128 (financial records); supplemented by the Companies (Registration of Companies) Regulations 1994 and the Companies (Fees) Regulations 2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); online corporate register at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Application for Registration of a Company, submitted electronically through the Companies Office online register; the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under section 17 of the Companies Act 1993 together with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The company must have at least one issued share under section 10(1)(a) of the Companies Act 1993. Shares may be issued for cash or non-cash consideration as fixed by the board of directors. No escrow arrangement, capital deposit account, or bank confirmation of paid-up capital is required under New Zealand law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED

DATE AND VENUE: [DATE] at the registered office, [PHYSICAL ADDRESS], NEW ZEALAND.

PRESENT: [DIRECTOR NAME] (Chairperson). IN ATTENDANCE: [INCORPORATION AGENT / COMPANY SECRETARY].

NOTED: The Company was incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 on [INCORPORATION DATE]; the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN have been received; consents of the directors have been filed with the Registrar of Companies.

RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION: That the initial subscriber be and is hereby recorded as the holder of [1] ordinary share in the share capital of the Company, subscribed at an issue price of NZD 1.00 per share, fully paid in cash. The board acknowledges that New Zealand imposes no minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit requirement and directs that the share register be updated accordingly.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE: That the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [PHYSICAL ADDRESS], New Zealand, being a physical address and not a postal box, and that the Registrar of Companies be notified of any change of registered office within the statutory period under section 15 of the Companies Act 1993.

3. APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS: That [DIRECTOR NAME] of [DIRECTOR ADDRESS] be and is hereby appointed as a director of the Company. The board confirms that at least one director is a natural person resident in New Zealand or in a jurisdiction recognised under an approved Memorandum of Understanding and that the director is not disqualified under Part 8 of the Companies Act 1993.

4. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: That [OFFICER NAME] be and is hereby appointed as Chief Executive Officer and Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer, with delegated authority to execute commercial agreements, engage professional advisers, and operate banking accounts in the ordinary course of business, subject to a two-signatory threshold for payments exceeding NZD 50,000.

5. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE: That the Company adopts its constitution as registered with the Companies Office; that board meetings be held at least quarterly; and that minutes, the share register, and financial records be maintained at the registered office in accordance with sections 23-25 and 128 of the Companies Act 1993.

6. BANKING AND PAYMENT RAILS: That the directors be and are hereby authorised to open and operate corporate bank accounts with New Zealand registered banks and to enable SWIFT Wire and ACH Direct settlement rails for the Company's programmatic advertising exchange and supply-side platform (SSP) transactions.

7. ACCOUNTANT AND AUDITOR: That [ACCOUNTING FIRM] be and is hereby appointed as external accountant/auditor, responsible for financial statements prepared in accordance with NZ IFRS, and that management implement a transfer pricing policy for cross-border platform services.

8. INDUSTRIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL LICENSING: That the board confirms that the Company's ISIC 7310 software and programmatic ad-exchange business is not subject to any industrial manufacturing licence, environmental impact assessment, or civil-defence operating permit in New Zealand, and directs management to maintain ongoing compliance with the Privacy Act 2020, the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007, the Fair Trading Act 1986, and the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.

CERTIFIED TRUE COPY.
[Signature]
[NAME], Chairperson
DATE: [DATE]

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Company Name Search portal (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz) and Intellectual Property Office of New Zealand (IPONZ) trade mark register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the Companies Register to confirm the proposed name is available and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name under sections 14 and 22 of the Companies Act 1993. Verify trade mark availability via IPONZ to avoid a passing-off risk. Choose a name ending with 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. Reserve the name electronically through the Companies Office online system; name reservations in New Zealand do not require notarization and are processed automatically.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name with up to three alternative names
Shareholder and director identity particulars (full legal name, residential address, date of birth)
Pre-incorporation NZBN checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is declined as identical or too similar, select an alternative name and re-file. If a third-party objection is raised under section 22, file a response with the Registrar within 20 working days or apply to the High Court under section 23 for a name direction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualified New Zealand legal counsel or licensed incorporation agent acting on behalf of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution or resolve that the default rules in the Companies Act 1993 apply. Obtain written consents of the proposed director and shareholder under section 13. Consents must be signed by hand or verified electronic signature; notarization is not mandatory under New Zealand law, but identity verification is required for Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT) compliance. Prepare the pro-forma first board resolution for execution after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Constitution (if adopted)
Signed consent to act as director
Signed consent of shareholder to take shares
Certified passport or national identity document of each director and shareholder
Proof of residential address for each director and shareholder (for AML/CFT know-your-customer verification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any consent is defective, re-execute and re-deliver to the incorporation agent. If a proposed director is not ordinarily resident in New Zealand, confirm eligibility under the Australian Memorandum of Understanding exemption or appoint an additional New Zealand-resident director to satisfy section 10(1)(b).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) — Online Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the electronic Form 1 Application for Registration of a Company through the Companies Office portal. Attach the constitution if adopted, confirm the physical registered office address in New Zealand, and upload the director and shareholder consents. Pay the statutory filing fee of NZD 100 (approximately USD 61) by debit or credit card. Approval is generally immediate where all statutory fields are complete and compliant.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1 (electronic)
Company constitution (attached where adopted)
Physical registered office address in New Zealand (not a P.O. Box)
Director and shareholder consents (uploaded in the application)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or requisition under sections 12 to 16, correct the indicated fields and re-submit within the requisition period. Where consent records are rejected, re-upload certified copies and re-file the affected pages.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful processing, the Registrar automatically issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the 13-digit New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Verify the registered particulars and request a correction under section 158 of the Companies Act 1993 if any detail is inaccurate. Download the certificate from the Companies Register for use in banking and tax registration.
required_dossiers: Company number and NZBN generated on the register
Certificate of Incorporation (downloadable PDF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate is not generated, contact the Companies Office helpdesk for manual issuance. If the NZBN is not automatically issued, apply through the NZBN website and cite the company number to synchronise records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Inland Revenue for tax obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NZBN, register the company for income tax and obtain an IRD number through the myIR online portal or Form IR596. Register for GST if taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 per annum. Confirm the tax-exempt zone treatment of the International Company designation and apply for any applicable withholding agent status. Provide New Zealand bank account details for refund accounts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
NZBN confirmation
Registered office address
Director and beneficial owner identification records
New Zealand bank account details for IRD refund account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD registration is delayed, contact the IRD Business Hotline or escalate via secure myIR correspondence. Submit a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation to resolve any entity verification mismatch.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain occupational safety, fire safety and building clearance for physical premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), territorial authority building consent authority, and WorkSafe New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the physical registered office, obtain and maintain a building Warrant of Fitness and current compliance schedule where the premises are non-residential. Register a fire evacuation scheme with FENZ if more than 10 persons work on site. File a general risk assessment and worker engagement plan under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for WorkSafe New Zealand inspection readiness.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or certificate of title for the registered office
Building compliance schedule or structural load certificate
Fire evacuation scheme application with floor plans
Workplace health and safety policy and risk register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the building has no code compliance certificate, commission a suitably qualified structural engineer to issue a building survey report and file an application with the territorial authority under the Building Act 2004 for a waiver or retrospective certification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand and the relevant Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the company's software-based programmatic advertising exchange and supply-side platform operations constitute an exclusively office-based activity that is exempt from environmental impact assessment licensing and resource consent requirements. No discharge permit is required; however, implement a written e-waste and ICT hardware disposal arrangement with a certified recycler in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.
required_dossiers: Environmental exemption declaration for office-based service activity
E-waste disposal contract with a certified recycler
Office waste management records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: No adverse action is anticipated. If a regional council query is received, submit a legal opinion confirming the exempt status and, if necessary, apply for a permitted activity certificate as a precaution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing licensing regime applies to ISIC 7310 (Advertising) in New Zealand. Sector oversight is exercised by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) and the Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) for voluntary commercial self-regulation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operating licence, facility permit, or manufacturing approval is required to operate a programmatic real-time advertising exchange and supply-side platform in New Zealand.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand and the relevant Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based digital service activity; no Schedule 4 activity under the Resource Management Act 1991; no resource consent or discharge permit required for software operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for software operations. General obligations under sections 15-17 of the Resource Management Act 1991 apply: no discharge of contaminants to air, land or water that causes adverse effects. E-waste and ICT hardware disposal must be handled by a certified recycler in compliance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 and applicable electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: building Warrant of Fitness and compliance schedule under the Building Act 2004, enforced by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; fire evacuation scheme registered with FENZ where on-site headcount exceeds 10 persons. Structural: premises must hold a code compliance certificate or acceptable structural load inspection report. Occupational: general risk assessment, worker participation system, and hazard controls under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, with notification to WorkSafe New Zealand where operations involve notifiable work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), Wellington, New Zealand; taxpayer portal: myIR (https://ird.govt.nz). Business entity registration infrastructure also includes the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Register (https://www.nzbn.govt.nz) and the New Zealand Companies Office for foreign company/branch registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident or foreign-incorporated International Company: (1) obtain an NZBN from the NZBN Register, including registration as an overseas company if a local branch or legal person is created; (2) apply to the Inland Revenue Department for a New Zealand IRD number (tax file number) using Form IR742 (non-resident company/non-resident tax registration), accompanied by certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, board resolution, director and controller details, foreign tax identification number, registered office/principal place of business information and a declaration of expected New Zealand tax nexus; (3) where taxable supplies will exceed the GST threshold, register for GST through myIR or Form GST-101A; the GST registration uses the same IRD number and no separate VAT registration number label is issued. A fully offshore tax-exempt International Company with no New Zealand taxable activity is not ordinarily required to register, but an IRD number may be obtained for withholding tax reporting if New Zealand-source payments will be made.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. A corporate International Company is treated as an entity-level taxpayer to the extent it derives New Zealand-source income through a fixed establishment or carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand. No general tax-exempt-zone election exists under New Zealand domestic law; any tax-exempt status must arise from the non-resident/offshore international-company regime. For controlled foreign company attribution, the statutory active income exclusion may be available; for hybrid mismatch arrangements, elections and timing adjustments may be required under the Taxation (Neutralising Hybrid Mismatch Arrangements) Act 2018, and binding rulings or private rulings are available under Part VA of the Tax Administration Act 1994.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory continuous transaction controls. E-invoicing is voluntary; the New Zealand GST Act 1985 permits electronic tax invoices provided they contain all prescribed particulars, including supplier name and GST number, date, description of supply, consideration, GST amount and zero-rated or exempt-supply indicators. New Zealand supports the Peppol PINT/UBL standard through the NZBN Peppol Authority, but there is no statutory obligation to use it or to clear invoices through an IRD API. Taxpayers must retain source documentation; the IRD may require read-only access to accounting systems during audit, but no automated fiscal clearance occurs for programmatic advertising or SSP supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (a) supplies of goods physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier or by the purchaser before the goods are used in New Zealand; (b) services supplied to a non-resident outside New Zealand where the services are not supplied to a New Zealand resident and not performed in connection with goods situated in New Zealand at the time the services are performed; and (c) certain international transport, telecommunications and supplies to inbound/outbound non-residents. Programmatic advertising, ad exchange and SSP services supplied to foreign counterparties will be zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident and the services are effectively consumed outside New Zealand; if the recipient is a New Zealand GST-registered business making taxable supplies, the supply may be zero-rated by way of the recipient's reverse-charge election rather than the supplier's export evidence. The exporter must hold contemporaneous documentary proof of export or non-resident performance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged with the New Zealand Customs Service
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing physical export movement from New Zealand and foreign destination
Commercial invoice and programmatic service agreement evidencing the offshore recipient and non-resident performance
Inward Remittance Certificate, Swift MT103 payment instruction or bank statement proving foreign currency consideration repatriated to a New Zealand bank account within the statutory period
GST return schedules, foreign exchange conversion records, ad-delivery/SSP logs, and foreign counterparty due diligence records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Incorrect zero-rating, fraudulent export claims, or failure to substantiate export/repatriation within the 180-day deadline will result in reversal of the zero rate and output GST at 15%, together with late payment penalties of up to 100% of the unpaid amount, use-of-money interest, and shortfall penalties of 20% for an unacceptable tax position, increasing to 150% for evasion. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994, deliberate tax evasion may be prosecuted criminally and can result in fines up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years; directors and controlling shareholders may be held personally liable. The IRD and New Zealand Customs Service jointly audit export-facing platforms; retrospective clawbacks may include the full 15% GST, penalties, and compound interest where the documentation bundle is incomplete or the foreign sales proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), with foreign direct investment screening administered by the Overseas Investment Office at Toitū Te Whenua / Land Information New Zealand under the Overseas Investment Act 2005; New Zealand maintains no comprehensive foreign exchange control statute.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalized capital and current account regime with a freely floating New Zealand dollar (NZD). The NZD is fully convertible for both current and capital account purposes; there are no residual surrender or conversion obligations and no central bank approval requirement for repatriation of profits, dividends, royalties, or intercompany settlements. Profit remittance is subject only to standard non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) at treaty-reduced rates on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties, plus standard documentation requirements under the Income Tax Act 2007. For an International Company with exempt-zone tax treatment, the assessable risk is substance, not exchange control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in New Zealand. Exporters and cross-border digital service providers may retain foreign currency proceeds offshore or in New Zealand foreign-currency accounts indefinitely, and may convert freely at market rates. The only applicable obligations are statistical reporting to Statistics New Zealand and record-keeping under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), including prescribed transaction reports for cash transactions at or above NZD 10,000 and wire-transfer record thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material structural constraints. An offshore digital EMI may service the New Zealand entity only if the EMI is registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers Act 2008, maintains membership in an approved dispute-resolution scheme, and complies with the AML/CFT Act when carrying on business in New Zealand. An unregulated offshore EMI without FSPR registration is not an acceptable sole treasury rail for an NZ-incorporated International Company and will generate adverse audit opinions, bank refusal of downstream correspondent wires, and regulator sanction risk. Where used, the EMI should be limited to settlement facilitation while the primary custody and operating accounts remain at a tier-1 NZ bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of directors is not a statutory prerequisite for account opening. The major New Zealand trading banks permit fully remote onboarding via video-verified KYC, encrypted passport scanning, and digital signature platforms, supported by certified true copies and independent source-of-funds verification. However, the banks retain absolute discretion to require an in-person interview when the beneficial ownership structure involves a non-resident tax-exempt International Company, offshore trustees, or layered custodians. In such cases, a registered New Zealand physical office, a locally licensed professional agent, and an apostilled director resolution materially expedite approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident International Company classified as Tax-Exempt Zone with no visible local operating substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, constitutional documents, register of directors and ultimate beneficial owners, board resolution authorizing account opening and permitted signatories, audited or management financial statements, evidence of commercial substance including a New Zealand registered office lease, local agent agreement, active advertising-technology contracts, and an organizational chart depicting the complete custody chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered trust or corporate beneficial ownership where the underlying natural persons are not immediately visible
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trust deed or custody agreement, current register of settlors, beneficiaries and protectors, passport copies of all natural persons holding or controlling 25% or more of the economic interest, a professional introducer letter from a reputable law or accounting firm, and a written legal opinion confirming actual ownership, control, and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity micro-payment flows to global DSP/SSP partners creating an unusual transaction profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed programmatic master services agreements with demand and supply platforms, platform credentials evidencing registered business users, approved invoice and payout schedules, a counterparty jurisdiction matrix compatible with sanctions screening, historical settlement-volume projections, and copies of applicable advertising-exchange licenses or platform self-regulatory certifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Deposits sourced from payment acquirers or money-service businesses generating potential third-party settlement risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A minimum of 12 months of clean source-bank statements, a director-signed source-of-funds declaration, underlying commercial contracts with advertising customers, confirmation that the funds are not sourced from unlicensed money transmitters, evidence that no sanctioned jurisdictions or blocked parties are involved, and a treasury policy demonstrating segregation of client and operational funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party shareholder loans or intra-group funding without a genuine treasury purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shareholder loan or intercompany agreements, board-approved transfer pricing documentation consistent with OECD and Inland Revenue (IRD) requirements, a detailed projected cash-flow and repayment schedule, confirmation that interest rates are arm's length, and a valid New Zealand IRD number or non-resident withholding tax declaration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is routed exclusively through New Zealand registered banks via SWIFT MT103 wires using standard transaction purpose codes: 'EQUITY' for paid-in share capital, 'LOAN' for shareholder advances, and 'DEBT' for intercompany treasury flows. No Reserve Bank of New Zealand exchange-control approval or conversion permit is required for a non-bank entity. The receiving bank performs sanctions screening, source-of-funds verification, and AML/CFT wire-format record-keeping. For share capital injections, a bank confirmation of the inward funds may be required for Companies Office solvency certification and to evidence the capital escrow release condition.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border trade settlements to advertising partners, media sellers, and inventory suppliers are cleared primarily via SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer messages denominated in USD, EUR, or NZD with same-day treasury execution from multicurrency accounts. Domestic NZD disbursements clear through the Bulk Electronic Clearing System (BECS)/ACH rails. For larger or structured settlements, Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 and documentary collections are available from the tier-1 banks, though they are uncommon for programmatic ad-tech flows. The treasury desk may deploy standing payment instructions for recurring SSP payout cycles.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards with maturity matching to inventory settlement cycles
FX Swaps for rolling offshore advertising working capital
Cross-Currency Swaps (XCCY) to match intercompany loan principal and interest exposure
Vanilla FX Options for premium-controlled downside protection
Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) accessible from global counterparty banks where a deliverable domestic NZD forward is operationally preferred

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (AR-2001) confirming registered office, directors, shareholders, and share allotments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the company's balance date (default balance date is the anniversary of incorporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of NZD 50 (approx. USD 30) applies; continued non-filing results in a notice of default and, after the statutory warning period, administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (if the company qualifies as a reporting entity under the Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months of the balance date, or within 20 working days after sign-off for listed or FMC reporting entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file can trigger an infringement fee of NZD 500 (approx. USD 300), director-level penalties, and possible application by the Registrar for court-ordered compliance or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Nil tax confirmation / annual non-resident declaration for tax-exempt International Company with no New Zealand-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Required only if New Zealand-source income arises; otherwise recorded internally and confirmed on the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incorrect or omitted filings can attract a late-filing penalty of up to NZD 250 per 30-day period and default assessment interest; continued failure may lead to non-compliance notices and enforced tax assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is mandatory if the company is an FMC reporting entity, has consolidated total assets exceeding NZD 60 million, has consolidated total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, or if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) as issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB) for reporting entities; non-reporting companies may prepare financial statements under the Framework for Differential Reporting and may use the Reduced Disclosure Regime where eligible.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual return confirms directors and all registered shareholders. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members at the time of transfer. No standalone public beneficial ownership filing is currently required for ordinary New Zealand companies; however, AML/CFT-regulated corporate services providers must refresh beneficial ownership identification at least annually.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (flat company tax rate under Income Tax Act 2007, s BC 18)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not provide corporate tax holidays or territorial exempt-zone preferential tax regimes. Available incentives include: 15% R&D Tax Credit for qualifying R&D activity; imputation credit system for resident shareholders; no separate provincial or municipal income tax; the Multinational Top-up Tax (Global Minimum Tax) applies from 2024/25 to large groups with annual consolidated revenue of €750 million or more. A non-resident International Company with no New Zealand fixed establishment is generally taxable only on New Zealand-sourced income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (subject to the 49% shareholder continuity requirement or the same-business continuity test under the Income Tax Act 2007)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Tax Return (for companies) filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal or via approved tax agent software. Non-resident and trustee companies may use IR4 with attachment schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual CIT return; provisional tax paid in three installments where residual income tax exceeds NZ$5,000. No quarterly CIT return is filed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard balance date of 31 March, the IR4 return is due by 7 July following the balance date. For a non-standard balance date, the due date is the 7th day of the 4th month after the balance date (e.g., 30 June balance date due 7 October). A tax agent extension may extend the due date for a limited period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable income derived from all sources before deductions, including New Zealand-sourced programmatic advertising, DSP/SSP fees, data services, and incidental revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident International Company should include only New Zealand-sourced income attributable to a fixed establishment or carried on in New Zealand. Income from offshore principals without a New Zealand PE should be excluded and may instead be subject to NRWT or remain outside NZ taxing jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business expenses incurred in earning assessable income, excluding capital items and non-deductible entertainment or penalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be allocated to New Zealand-sourced gross income. Related-party service fees must be at arm's length and substantiated by transfer pricing documentation. No deduction is allowed for amounts subject to NRWT unless the payee is a registered approved issuer and the required withholding obligation is satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before loss carry-forwards, reconciled with financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the New Zealand branch/PE accounts with the global accounts. Any internal cost allocations, overhead recharges, and ad-tech platform charges must conform to the OECD authorised OECD approach (AOA) and arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year net loss brought forward from prior years under the loss continuity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forward is permitted indefinitely only if the same business is carried on and at least 49% continuity of ownership is maintained. For a non-resident IC controlled by a shareholder restructure, the loss claim may be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deduction of available loss carry-forwards and before application of tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate tax at 28% on taxable income attributable to New Zealand-sourced business. Claim treaty benefits only where the DTA grants NZ taxing rights to the residence state, and attach a completed IR4B or treaty relief statement if required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Core income tax liability at 28% on Box 5 taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC paying dividends, interest, or royalties out of New Zealand-source income, NRWT payment obligations are separate and not satisfied by the IR4 income tax liability. Imputation credits cannot confer a refund to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Tax credits (RWT, provisional tax, foreign tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for resident withholding tax paid, provisional tax paid, and any foreign tax credits available under the DTA.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC may claim provisional tax installments paid and any foreign tax credits under an applicable DTA for income also taxed in New Zealand. No imputation credits are available to a non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Refund or tax to pay
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance of tax after deducting all credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund is issued only after IRD verifies the non-resident's tax residence certificate and the branch's economic substance. Overpaid NRWT on cross-border distributions must be claimed through specific IRD refund procedures, not this box.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of NZ$250 for the IR4 return, with subsequent automatic NZ$250 penalties for each month or part-month the return remains unfiled up to a maximum of NZ$2,500, plus late payment penalties (1% per month, capped at 10%) and use-of-money interest (UOMI) at 8.35% per annum compounded daily. Criminal liability can arise for habitual failure to file or for filing a false return.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% standard non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends paid to non-residents; reduced to 15% for fully imputed dividends. Lower treaty rates may apply, commonly 15% under most comprehensive double tax agreements and 5% under certain treaties (e.g., Australia for significant shareholdings).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a certificate of tax residence from its home jurisdiction's competent authority; (ii) submit the certificate to the New Zealand payer (or IRD) before the withholding date; (iii) complete the relevant IRD withholding/certificate form (commonly IR3NR or the payer's non-resident declaration); and (iv) retain the certificate and supporting documentation in New Zealand for 7 years. If NRWT has been over-withheld, a refund application may be made through IRD's foreign taxpayer refund process after issuance of a tax assessment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest and royalties is 15% each. Applicable treaty rates commonly reduce interest withholding to 10% or 0% under certain DTAs, and royalties to 5% or 0% depending on the treaty and IP characterisation. Where the New Zealand payer is an approved issuer for foreign currency debt, the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may apply to interest in lieu of NRWT, provided the lender is not associated with the borrower and meets the approval conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Local File / Master File equivalent) must be prepared and retained where the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions with non-resident associated enterprises exceeds NZ$10 million in the relevant income year; country-by-country (CbC) reporting is required for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of NZ$1 billion or more, aligned with the OECD Pillar One/Two thresholds.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Profit Split Method (incl. transactional profit split)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to zero-tax offshore centres, but substantive business presence is a core requirement through the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA 2007 s BG1), the place-of-effective-management test, and transfer pricing rules. An International Company structured as a pure mailbox or SSP/DSP conduit with no New Zealand office, no local employees, no strategic board decisions taken in New Zealand, and no alignment of profit with actual risk-taking and commercial activity will be disregarded or recharacterised, with all income reallocated to the jurisdiction where the real economic functions, assets, and risks sit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting New Zealand-source programmatic advertising revenue from the IR4 return, fabricating management fees payable to a shell affiliate in a zero-tax jurisdiction, or using the New Zealand IC to conceal the true economic owner of an AdTech exchange/SSP platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the unpaid tax for evasion or an abusive tax position, plus late payment penalties and use-of-money interest. Criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 1994 s 143B: on conviction, a fine of up to NZ$50,000 for an individual and up to NZ$200,000 for a company, and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. Repeat offenders face higher fines and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly file false returns or cause tax avoidance are personally liable for shortfall penalties; IRD may issue a departure prohibition order under the Tax Administration Act preventing the director from leaving New Zealand while tax debts exist. Directors may also be sued for civil restitution for amounts diverted from the company, disqualified from managing companies under the Companies Act 1994, and, upon criminal conviction, imprisoned as principals or parties to the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company with no physical New Zealand presence, no employees or directors resident in New Zealand, no board meetings or commercial substance in New Zealand, and no transfer pricing documentation despite related-party transactions exceeding the NZ$10 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the arrangement under the general anti-avoidance rule; transfer pricing adjustments increasing New Zealand taxable income; denial of treaty benefits if the residence claim is a sham or the entity is not beneficial owner; penalties of up to 150% for gross carelessness or abusive tax position; cancellation of tax registration and potential strike-off under the Companies Act 1994 for no real business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the company's unpaid PAYE, GST, and certain penalties under director penalty notice rules; for income tax, personal liability attaches where the director has caused the company to evade tax or has assisted in a sham arrangement. Courts may pierce the corporate veil to order civil restitution to corporate creditors and IRD; directors can face travel bans, disqualification, and criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering and Unlicensed Payment Routing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting programmatic ad proceeds through layered SWIFT/ACH wires, using shell accounts in low-tax jurisdictions, failing to perform customer due diligence on ad counterparties, or deliberately obscuring the ownership structure of the AdTech exchange to avoid anti-money laundering scrutiny.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a reporting entity that fails to conduct adequate customer due diligence, collection, or verification controls, or that knowingly facilitates money laundering, is liable on conviction to large fines: up to NZ$2 million for a body corporate and NZ$300,000 for an individual, plus potential imprisonment of up to 2 years. Non-reporting evasion of the AML/CFT regime carries corresponding criminal penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, AML compliance officers, and senior managers are personally liable if they knowingly allow tainted funds to move through the platform. Penalties include personal fines up to NZ$300,000, imprisonment up to 2 years, civil forfeiture orders, extradition and travel bans, and disqualification from holding directorships. Company directors cannot shelter behind corporate immunity where they were the controlling mind of the money laundering operation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement / Cross-Border Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Invoicing IP royalties, software licence fees, or management recharges at a non-arm's length rate between the New Zealand IC and its foreign parent/affiliates, or allocating profits away from New Zealand-sourced ad-tech revenue without functional, asset, and risk analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment under Part IV of the Income Tax Act 2007, added tax, shortfall penalties up to 150% for evasion-like behaviour or 40% for gross carelessness, and daily late payment interest. If the adjustment creates an understatement of taxable income exceeding NZ$100,000, the taxpayer may be subject to a penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall for an abusive tax position.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign inaccurate transfer pricing disclosure certificates or cause the company to enter into structured arrangements to defeat the arm's length principle can be personally liable for penalties and interest. In severe cases, directors may be criminally prosecuted for evasion of tax, banned from leaving New Zealand under departure prohibition orders, and required to personally reimburse the company for tax penalties and losses through civil proceedings.
